source: 我不想再努力了，我要躺平。
intended_meaning: I don't want to keep pushing myself; I'm opting out of the rat race.
raw_translation: I don't want to try anymore. I'm going to lay flat.
refined: I don't want to put in any more effort; I'm just going to lie flat.
reason: "躺平" is a specific Chinese slang term meaning to opt out of the rat race or stop striving for success (often translated as "lying flat"); while "lay flat" captures the literal action, adding context like "put in any more effort" clarifies the intended idiom rather than just describing a physical posture.

source: 现在工作太卷了，我想躺平。
intended_meaning: Work is so cutthroat now that I just want to opt out.
raw_translation: Now the job's too curly, I'd like to lay flat.
refined: Work is way too competitive now; I want to lie flat.
reason: "卷" refers to intense workplace competition/hustle culture, not literally "curly"; "躺平" is a specific slang term for opting out of the rat race/lying flat that needs cultural adaptation rather than literal translation

source: 我们公司太内卷了，大家都加班到十点。
intended_meaning: My company is hyper-competitive; everyone works overtime until 10.
raw_translation: We're too introverted. We're all working till 10:00.
refined: Our company is way too competitive; everyone works until ten.
reason: 内卷 refers to intense internal competition/involution in a workplace context, not introversion

source: 看到那个视频我直接破防了。
intended_meaning: That video hit me hard emotionally.
raw_translation: I just broke it when I saw that video.
refined: I was so emotionally affected by that video.
reason: 破防 is internet slang meaning being emotionally overwhelmed or having one's defenses broken; translated literally as breaking an object

source: 我是社恐，不想去那个聚会。
intended_meaning: I'm socially anxious/awkward, so I don't want to go to that party.
raw_translation: I'm scared. I don't want to go to that party.
refined: I have social anxiety, so I don't want to go to that party.
reason: 社恐 is an abbreviation for 社交恐惧症 (social phobia/social anxiety); translated literally as 'scared' loses the specific meaning

source: 打工人又要上班了。
intended_meaning: Back to the grind again (self-deprecating joke about being a worker).
raw_translation: Beating the workers is going to work again.
refined: It's time for another day at the office.
reason: "打工" refers to being an employee or working a job, not "beating workers"; literal translation creates a violent and incorrect meaning

source: 别凡尔赛了，你明明考得很好。
intended_meaning: Stop humblebragging, you obviously did great on the exam.
raw_translation: Oh, come on, Versailles. You did a great job.
refined: Stop being humble-bragging; you clearly aced the exam.
reason: 凡尔赛 is internet slang for 'humble-brag'; translation used literal place name

source: 他对考试很佛系。
intended_meaning: He's very laid-back about exams and doesn't stress.
raw_translation: He's very Buddhist in his exams.
refined: He is very laid-back about the exam.
reason: "fó xì" (buddhist) here means relaxed or indifferent; literal "Buddhist" translation misses the intended meaning of being chill

source: 我就是来吃瓜的。
intended_meaning: I'm just here to watch the drama.
raw_translation: I'm here to eat melons.
refined: I'm just here for the drama.
reason: "eating melon" is an idiom meaning watching gossip or a spectacle; literal translation misses the intended meaning

source: 这个价格太离谱了。
intended_meaning: This price is ridiculous.
raw_translation: This price is ridiculous.
refined: This price is outrageous.
reason: 离谱 implies something unreasonable or absurd in a way that 'outrageous' captures better than the neutral 'ridiculous', though both are acceptable; keeping it close to source tone

source: 这个游戏太上头了。
intended_meaning: This game is so addictive.
raw_translation: This game is too high.
refined: This game is so addictive.
reason: "上头" in this context means being highly engaging or addictive; the literal translation "too high" misses the intended meaning.

source: 这家火锅yyds！

raw_translation: This fire potyds!
refined: This hotpot is yyds!
reason: "fire pot" is a mistranslation of "huoguo" (hotpot); kept the slang acronym "yyds" as it is commonly understood in English-speaking contexts familiar with Chinese internet culture.

source: 我今天有点emo。
intended_meaning: I'm feeling kind of down today.
raw_translation: I'm a little emo today.
refined: I've been feeling down today.
reason: "emo" is internet slang for being sad or emotionally unstable; translating it literally as the noun "emo" sounds unnatural in standard English.

source: 这个菜绝了！

reason: "绝了" in this context expresses extreme praise or excitement about the food; "perfect" misses the colloquial intensity and specific reference to a dish.
